summary.one_liner: L2MAC is a Python framework that uses LLM agents as a stored-program computer with a file store, so one prompt can produce output (such as a full codebase or book) larger than the model's context window.
summary.what_it_does: L2MAC takes a single natural-language prompt and generates a self-bootstrapped "prompt-program," a sequence of instruction steps. Each step runs in a fresh LLM agent whose context is managed by a control unit. The agents read and write a persistent file store that holds intermediate and final outputs, so the total output is not limited by the context window. For coding tasks, it can also check generated code for syntax errors and run unit tests, feeding errors back for correction. It is usable as a CLI (`l2mac "..."`) or as a Python library (`generate_codebase`), and writes results to a ./workspace folder. The README reports benchmark results on large codebase generation and HumanEval (90.2% Pass@1) and includes examples such as a snake game, a URL shortener web app, a blackjack CLI, and a pasta recipe book.
use_cases: generate a complete codebase from one prompt
automatically write a long book or recipe book
build a small pygame game from a description
produce large multi-file software projects with an LLM
research long-form LLM output generation beyond context limits
run LLM agents with persistent file-based memory
how_to_run: conda create -n l2mac python=3.9 && conda activate l2mac
Edit ~/.l2mac/config.yaml with llm api_type, model, base_url and api_key
l2mac "Create a beautiful, playable and simple snake game with pygame."
stack: OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs (configurable api_type, default gpt-4o in example config)
notable: Stored-program design: each instruction step runs in a new LLM agent with tools to read and write a persistent file store
Self-generated prompt-program bootstrapped from a one-line prompt, or user-supplied
Generates unit tests alongside code and uses failing tests and syntax errors to drive self-correction
Usable as both a CLI and a Python library (generate_codebase)
caveats: Requires access to an LLM API key and its costs; the example config uses gpt-4o
Setup details are referenced in external docs and the README does not fully describe the QuickStart section
Benchmark claims come from the paper's own evaluations (averaged over 10 seeds)
